introduction: In Illyria, a shipwrecked young woman enters a duke's service disguised as a man and becomes the messenger for a love she wishes were directed towards herself. Her errands disturb a household where mourning, drinking, music and social ambition compete for attention. Wit can express hidden feeling or turn another person's confidence against them, and an absent twin makes appearances still harder to interpret. The play follows several kinds of desire through disguises that offer protection while creating fresh vulnerability.

fullSynopsis.text: Shipwrecked in Illyria, Viola fears that her twin brother Sebastian has drowned. With a sea captain's help she disguises herself as a young man, Cesario, and enters Duke Orsino's service. Orsino loves Olivia, who refuses his suit while mourning her brother. He sends Cesario to plead for him, unaware that Viola has fallen in love with him herself. Her spirited embassy instead attracts Olivia, who invents a story about a forgotten ring to secure another meeting. Viola recognises the resulting triangle but cannot see how to untangle it.

In Olivia's household, her uncle Sir Toby encourages the foolish Sir Andrew Aguecheek to continue his hopeless courtship and finance their drinking. The steward Malvolio rebukes their noisy revelry with Feste the fool. Maria retaliates by forging a letter in Olivia's handwriting, exploiting Malvolio's self-love and desire for advancement. Already imagining himself Olivia's husband and Toby's superior, he interprets its hints as proof of her love. Hidden spectators enjoy his decision to obey its instructions: smile continually, wear yellow stockings cross-gartered, and treat others with haughty disdain. These are precisely the gestures Olivia will dislike.

Sebastian has survived, rescued by Antonio, whose devotion leads him to follow the young man despite enemies in Orsino's territory. Antonio lends Sebastian his purse and arranges lodgings while Sebastian explores. Meanwhile Viola continues to serve Orsino's courtship, answering his claims about women's lesser capacity for love with a disguised account of her own unspoken passion. Olivia confesses her love directly to Cesario, but Viola rejects it. Toby and Fabian persuade the jealous Andrew to challenge Cesario, then terrify each reluctant combatant with invented reports of the other's ferocity. Toby privately expects further profit from Andrew's fear.

Following the forged letter, Malvolio appears before Olivia smiling and extravagantly dressed. She believes him deranged and entrusts his care to her household. The plotters exploit that concern to confine him in darkness. Feste impersonates the curate Sir Topas, denying Malvolio's perceptions and making irrational demands as tests of sanity, before promising writing materials for an appeal. During the threatened duel, Antonio mistakes Viola for Sebastian and intervenes to protect her. Officers arrest him. When Viola cannot return a purse she never received, Antonio believes Sebastian has betrayed him; his accusations give Viola fresh hope that her brother lives.

Andrew next attacks the real Sebastian, who fights back and also resists Toby. Olivia intervenes, calls him Cesario and invites him home. Astonished by her affection and gifts, Sebastian accepts his good fortune, though he cannot explain it. He agrees to accompany her and a priest to make a secret marriage contract. When Orsino arrives with Viola, Antonio repeats his charge of ingratitude, Olivia claims Cesario as her husband, and the priest confirms their recent ceremony. Orsino believes his favourite has deceived him. The wounded knights add accusations of violence that Viola truthfully denies.

Sebastian's arrival allows the twins to compare their family memories and recognise each other. Olivia discovers which sibling she has contracted herself to, while Orsino offers Viola his hand and promises marriage. Her female clothes remain with the captain, now imprisoned at Malvolio's suit, so their recovery and the public celebrations are still to come. Malvolio's letter brings his treatment to light. Olivia recognises Maria's forgery, and Fabian admits the plot, reporting that Toby has married Maria. Feste renews the mockery; Malvolio leaves threatening revenge. Orsino orders an effort at reconciliation, which is not completed. Antonio's legal fate is unstated. Feste ends the play with a song about life's persistent wind and rain.

acts.label: ACT I.
acts.summary: Orsino indulges his passion for Olivia, whose mourning for her brother excludes his suit. Viola arrives after a shipwreck, uncertain whether her twin has survived, and asks the captain to conceal her identity and help her enter the duke's service in male disguise. At Olivia's house, Maria criticises Sir Toby's drinking and his encouragement of the foolish suitor Sir Andrew. Viola, now Cesario, becomes Orsino's trusted messenger while secretly loving him. Feste challenges Olivia's solemnity and Malvolio's self-regard. Cesario gains an audience and pleads eloquently for Orsino, but Olivia falls for the messenger instead. She sends Malvolio after Cesario with a ring and a fabricated explanation.

acts.label: ACT II.
acts.summary: Sebastian reveals his identity and grief for his apparently drowned sister to Antonio, who rescued him. Antonio resolves to follow him despite danger in Orsino's territory. Malvolio's delivery of Olivia's ring makes Viola realise that Olivia loves Cesario. In the household, Malvolio interrupts Toby, Andrew and Feste's late-night singing; Maria plans revenge through a forged love letter. Orsino sends Viola back to Olivia after a conversation in which Viola describes her own concealed love as a sister's history. Maria plants the letter while Toby, Andrew and Fabian hide nearby. Malvolio's fantasies of marriage and authority make him accept its ambiguous clues and instructions about dress, smiling and behaviour.

acts.label: ACT III.
acts.summary: Olivia openly declares her love for Cesario, who insists that no woman can possess his heart. Toby and Fabian keep Andrew from abandoning his suit by urging him to challenge his rival. Antonio explains his danger in the city and lends Sebastian his purse. Malvolio's obedience to Maria's letter convinces Olivia that he is mad; the plotters plan dark confinement. Toby then frightens Viola and Andrew into an unwilling duel by exaggerating each one's skill and anger. Antonio interrupts, believing Viola is Sebastian, and is arrested. His demand for the purse baffles Viola, whose genuine ignorance he reads as betrayal. His use of Sebastian's name revives her hope.

acts.label: ACT IV.
acts.summary: Feste mistakes Sebastian for Cesario, and Andrew attacks the wrong twin. Sebastian beats him and challenges Toby's restraint. Olivia stops the quarrel, addresses Sebastian as Cesario and takes him into her house, where her favour astonishes him. Meanwhile Maria dresses Feste as the curate Sir Topas to torment the imprisoned Malvolio. The fool disputes the darkness of his cell and refuses to recognise his sanity. Toby, worried about Olivia's displeasure, wants to end the prank. In his own voice Feste promises Malvolio light and writing materials. Sebastian cannot find Antonio but accepts Olivia's invitation to make a secret contract before a priest, promising to remain true.

acts.label: ACT V.
acts.summary: Orsino arrives with Viola, and Antonio accuses Cesario of abandoning his rescuer. Olivia's declaration that Cesario is her husband, confirmed by the priest, makes Orsino condemn his supposed favourite's deceit. Andrew and Toby also blame Viola for Sebastian's blows. Sebastian appears, and the twins establish their identities through shared memories. Orsino promises to marry Viola, whose clothes remain with the imprisoned captain. Malvolio is released and produces the forged letter. Olivia identifies Maria's hand; Fabian confesses the plot and reports Toby's marriage to Maria. Malvolio vows revenge, leaving reconciliation unfinished. The promised celebrations and recovery of Viola's clothes lie ahead. Feste sings of recurring hardship as the play closes.
